name: Reno
tagline: No State Income Tax, Lake Tahoe Access, and High-Desert Adventure
description: Reno has reinvented itself from a casino town into a thriving hub for outdoor enthusiasts and tech workers. Nevada's zero state income tax is a massive draw for FIRE retirees, and Lake Tahoe is just 45 minutes away. The city offers over 300 days of sunshine, a growing food and arts scene, and access to world-class skiing, hiking, and mountain biking. Housing costs have risen but remain well below neighboring California, making Reno a compelling tax-advantaged base for the financially independent.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – safe in most neighborhoods; standard city precautions downtown
quickFacts.climate: Semi-arid high desert with four seasons; dry summers, snowy winters, and 300+ sunny days

housing.description: A modest studio or one-bedroom in Midtown, along Wells Avenue, or in nearby Sparks — at the studio average, above Las Vegas on California-spillover demand

dining.description: Home cooking and casual Midtown taquerias and cafes

healthcare.description: A subsidized individual plan through Nevada Health Link, assuming annual income stays under the federal subsidy cutoff of about $62,600. Priced for an early retiree aged 45-55; older retirees should budget more.

transportation.description: A paid-off AWD used car with NV insurance and gas — essential for daily life and the run to Tahoe

entertainment.description: Sierra-foothill hiking, Truckee River walks, and free Midtown art walks

1M.lifestyle: A practical high-desert life anchored by a modest studio or one-bedroom in Midtown, along Wells Avenue, or in nearby Sparks. A paid-off car is essential for daily errands and the 45-minute run to Lake Tahoe, with all-wheel drive earning its keep on snowy winter roads. Meals lean on home cooking and casual Midtown taquerias and cafes, while hiking in the Sierra foothills, walks along the Truckee River, and free Midtown art walks keep recreation cheap. Nevada's zero state income tax helps, and over 300 days of sunshine plus world-class mountains sit at the doorstep — though California-driven rent increases make this a disciplined budget.

3M.lifestyle: A comfortable life in a nice two-bedroom or a small house in Southwest Reno, Somersett, or Caughlin Ranch with Sierra views. Ski passes at Mt. Rose and Tahoe resorts, regular dining at places like Campo and The Depot, and a late-model SUV that handles mountain roads year-round all fit comfortably, alongside solid private health insurance. Lake Tahoe becomes a routine weekend destination, and Nevada's zero income tax saves meaningfully versus neighboring California. An outdoor-oriented base with real breathing room in the budget.

10M.lifestyle: The top of what Reno offers, anchored by a luxury custom home in a gated community like Montreux, ArrowCreek, or Caughlin Ranch with panoramic Sierra and valley views. A private chef, multiple luxury all-wheel-drive vehicles, full household help with landscaping and seasonal snow removal, concierge medicine, and top-tier ski passes are all routine, alongside first-class travel and regular Tahoe lakefront weekends. Reno's luxury ceiling is more modest than a coastal metro's, but zero state income tax on every withdrawn dollar makes it one of the most tax-efficient places in the country to hold a large portfolio.
